text_fidelity_a:
Patriot LX Series 64GB High Speed Micro SDXC Class 10 UHS-I Transfer Speeds For Action Cameras, Phones, Tablets, and PCs So I bought this to use with my 128GB Lenovo Yoga as a secondary drive. When I plugged it into my computer to transfer some files, it shows 116GBs - what it should be for a 128GB drive. Though I really wish computers and manufacturers would calculate memory the same, that is another matter.

I went to transfer a folder with 61 GBs of memory. It got about 3/4 done and it decided it was full. With about 50GBs, my 116 GB card is FULL. It should be only about half full. This is a problem. I am not happy about this and will not buy another one of these. I will format it and try again. Maybe there are hidden files that aren't showing up on it. But this is really annoying.

Update: I decided to format the drive and found that the bit size for exFAT is very small. As in less than my file size small. I changed it to NTSF, as it will only be used in a computer, and it is now working properly as regards to being able to actually fill it with 116 GBs. But it still took about 4 hours to copy 8 GBs of data to it. My USB 3.0 drive would have done it in less than 30 minutes.
text_fidelity_b: Patriot LX Series 64GB High Speed Micro SDXC Class 10 UHS-I Transfer Speeds For Action Cameras, Phones, Tablets, and PCs

Sound Storm Labs SMC90BB Sound System Weatherproof Bluetooth Amplifier 3 Inch Speakers Inline Volume Control Ideal for Motorcycles ATV and 12 Volt Applications My husband put this on one of the farm Polaris CUV's since installation is beyond what I would able to do. He was able to install it on a ranger using the roof system as the mounting position for the speakers. It installed easily enough - basically clamp the speaker to the roof support bars, make sure to use the included rubber strips to get these to clamp securely or you will be remounting these with the rubber strips again once they slide down. Wiring was simple as it all goes to one plug that attaches to the amp. This does mean you will be mounting all 4 speakers. And since the wiring is together in a harness, some thought is required as to where you put the speakers and a good route to where you want the amp installed. The amp install is simple as it basically needs power (12vdc) and not a lot else. It does come with a handy audio input jack so you can use something like an old iPod for audio input. It also has BNC inputs if you have say a radio that you would want to connect to it so there is some flexibility there. The Bluetooth hook up was simple and works well, but again do not hide the amp behind a lot of metal or this may not work to well.

As far as fit and finish, the only thing I can knock this on is the quality of the clamping hardware finish, but being on a rough duty vehicle this is actually okay.

The bottom line is: Overall installation is simple, and the unit is easy to use.
text_fidelity_b: Sound Storm Labs SMC90BB Sound System Weatherproof Bluetooth Amplifier 3 Inch Speakers Inline Volume Control Ideal for Motorcycles ATV and 12 Volt Applications

Garmin nüvi 1390/1390T 4.3-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I first became enamored of the garmin company after using the one with a rental car. The ease of use and accuracy was impressive. Unfortunately, that model is no longer in production so I opted for this unit.

In general I am pleased. Easy to set up, the unit features a bright, clear screen. It is a snap to use and the directions have been unfailing accurate. I drive alot and so far have used this unit throughout New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Maryland, DC and Virginia. I have had no problem with reception even while traversing mountainous regions. I appreciate the advance notice for turns and the voice command system is a convenience.

However, this unit is not flawless. The robotic voice often mispronounces street names and the voice command system seems a bit hard of hearing when it comes to addresses. I have had to pull over and type in the address. The unit does not like to deviate from its chosen route. For instance, one location I frequent in New York is accessible both by the thruway (toll road) and other non-toll main arteries. Both are about the same distance. When I want to avoid the toll route, the unit will recalculate directing that I turn around and follow the initial route multiple times before adjusting to the alternate route. A big deal, no,but annoying nonetheless. While I have not been terribly plagued by the pop ups, they are annoying and potentially unsafe. While the start up guide and manual are adequate, they are barely so. Whatever happened to detailed instructions? But my biggest gripe is the customer service. I called twice with questions and had ridicualously long waits of fifteen minutes and twenty-five minutes respectively. There is no round the clock service. The last time I called it wasnt even available all week, totally unacceptable.

So while I like this system,there is room for improvement.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 1390/1390T 4.3-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Belkin 6-Outlet Surge Protector with 3-Foot Cord (Plus An Extra 6-Foot Extension Cord) I'm confused. I thought when I got this surge suppressor that the extension cord was meant to be used with it so you'd have a total of nine feet of cord if needed. Apparently, the extension cord doesn't actually fit the surge suppressor; the extension cord has three two-prong receptacles that you could plug, say, lamps and the like into, but you cannot plug the surge suppressor itself into it. The extension cord is clearly marked as being for two-wire polarized, as opposed to three-prong grounded, appliances. So that's more than a little misleading.

The surge suppressor looks heavy-duty, but you are cautioned in the packaging literature that it's not to be used with "sensitive equipment" like everything we use surge suppressors for: computers, TV, etc. You can't use it with things involving water, either, like aquariums. So what would I use it for? A blow dryer? I think not. To make it even worse, you are told to cover the receptacles on the extension cord if they are not in use. There are little plastic sliders that you're supposed to use for this purpose. But one of the sliders on the extension cord I received won't stay closed. China-cheap.

Belkin has some good products, but this one doesn't impress me very much. And the whole thing is packaged in one of those awful clamshells that you risk hurting yourself on when you take the scissors to it.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin 6-Outlet Surge Protector with 3-Foot Cord (Plus An Extra 6-Foot Extension Cord)

Downloading books is absolutely a breeze and the selection of titles (for a premier launch of a product) is simply outstanding. I cannot wait to see what else will be added in the future and my credit card is ready and waiting.

Figuring out how to use the Kindle was easier than figuring out my basic LG cellphone. I am, obviously, a technical loser, but the Kindle has made me feel like a genius. And the instruction manual makes everything logical and simple to do - layed out for the quickest access. You don't feel intimidated or stupid when attempting to look something up.

My only complaint is that I wish there were some way of locking the right side "turn page" function. Unfortunately I have had to learn to grab my Kindle from the top and bottom because if I handle it from the sides, I will end up rapidly changing pages. And I know better than to lean it against anything on the right or left side for the same reason.

This the best Christmas gift I could have hoped for. I am now in the process of reading 6 different books, with 2 more in the queue. Not to mention 3 blogs which I check throughout the day.

The Kindle has opened up new worlds for me and is giving me the opportunity to discover subjects that I would never have considered in a million years. And why not? Instead of stacking books throughout my house, I can now carry them around in a compact unit which is lighter than a paperback.

I don't know who to thank for this wonderful creation, but I can assure you that I will be a customer for life.
text_fidelity_b: Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th)

I had to use the app because my AP doesn't have WPS and I wasn't immediately certain whether this would have an IP address or not. TP-Link AV2000 Powerline Adapter - 2 Gigabit Ports, Plug&Play(TL-PA9020 KIT),White I was expecting a bigger performance bump with the MIMO technology. I have been using TP-Link AV1200 3 ports with electric outlet pass throughs, but I was willing to lose the outlets and one port for better performance. It is a bit better - and the powerline upstairs is in an area that gets zero wifi connectivity - but we are still talking 15-20 Mbps, where I get well over 100 on my wifi downstairs.

I'm not convinced that this is the fault of the product. The rooms are all on different circuits - sometimes different circuits within the same room. Canon EF 100mm f/2.8 Macro USM Fixed Lens for Canon SLR Cameras Although this lens is intended for macro photography, it's also a great lens for general purpose shots, or portrait shots. The lens produces beautiful sharp images and is a fast, accurate focuser. The lens is moderately heavy and bulky, so I wouldn't classify it as eminently carryable, and without image stabilization, you might suffer hand shake blur if you're not shooting at the wide end; at smaller apertures, using it with a tripod is highly recommended. But if you're buying it primarily to get into macro this shouldn't much matter as tripod shooting with macro is virtually a necessity, and completely expected.

The 100mm focal length is a nice compromise when you want to get close to small subjects (particularly insects) but are limited to how close you can get before scaring the subject off - as a comparison with the 180mm macro, you would want to factor in a consideration as to what you might like to shoot most of the time - big spiders that you'd rather stay well away from might be an application more suited to the 180mm, for instance, but if you are keen to shoot mostly flowers, the 180 might be more length than you really need.

In short, the 100mm macro is one of my "keeper" lenses, a real performer.
text_fidelity_b: Canon EF 100mm f/2.8 Macro USM Fixed Lens for Canon SLR Cameras

Amped REC15A Wireless High Power Compact 802.11AC Wi-Fi Range Extender Among the wireless extenders, I have used, this model from Amped has been the easiest to set up, and it works as good as advertised. Using an iPad, it took less than 5 minutes to set up. Very intuitive and well-thought through interface for setting up with very clear information on each screen (an accurate countdown warns you exactly when to expect next steps, etc.). Overall, this has been the most pleasant experience in setting up any electronics gadget that is device-agnostic.

The performance is excellent; in a far away sunroom, the extender easily resulted in a "full" indicator for WiFi devices, and the ethernet port enabled to connect a gaming device (for very infrequent use, this will work very well; I already have an extended port to connect to the TV). The extender has performed consistently as well, no pauses in video streaming, for example.

There is one minor disadvantage, other than what seems to be a tad pricey - the bulk of the unit. It is difficult to place this in plug points with tight corners or abutting walls. I have had mixed experience in trying to print from a device connected to the extended network to a printer on the original network (need to verify settings and will update the review). Overall, an excellent choice for an extender+port option that is extremely easy to set up and works consistently.

Maybe, it's because I grew up in the 80s era, when there was real music and it had lots of bass, and I still want a lot of it. This speaker just doesn't have quite enough for me, but I still really like it. It is a bit taller and skinnier than a couple of older echo dots, and it doesn't have the same exact quality of sound, but sounds pretty darn good.
The color-changing light effect is pretty cool, but I wish there was a way to turn it off sometimes. Because I'm using it as a computer speaker most of the day, and it's a bit bothersome.
This little speaker packs a pretty good punch, aside from needing a bit more bass, and not being able to turn the light off. It will work great for times when you need a pretty loud sound source and have little room for a big speaker. It's small, has a slot for an SD card for playing your own playlist, it's rechargeable, and lasts for a good while before needing to be recharged. I would definitely recommend it!

Images are in color with more flexibility the Kindle reader on my Mac and I guess that's what I expected, only smaller. If I were only reading fiction, and image quality was not important I would probably keep it rather than go through the hassle of returning it.

As a technical writer I cannot imagine creating such an unfriendly and unwieldy interface. Opened the box less than an hour ago and the "user manual" on the Kindle evidently doesn't have a way to exit the manual or even get back to the the beginning without endlessly pressing the left side of the screen one screen page at a time. Worse yet after after endless "left tapping" I am getting close to the beginning of the manual I am taken forward again to a chapter near the end of the manual. Insane! I just want to get out of the manual or at least access the tool bar and am unable to do so . Supposedly tapping the top of the page allows access to the tool bar but all that does is highlight a word at the top of the page. What's up with this? So far extremely disappointed and frustrated. Nothing should be this difficult. While writing this review the screen changed to the cover and blurb of a book and the Kindle is frozen on that page. By the way, image is dark as is the entire page. It just keeps getting better, folks. Hopefully a restart will remove the kinks and won't be a total waste of money, time and effort. If not this is Kindle is useless and going back. If things improve I will update.

text_fidelity_a:
ZyXEL 300 Mbps Wireless N Access Point, Ethernet Client, Universal Repeater, and Range Extender (WAP3205) Overall this is a good little feature-rich device but use just the wireless access point features. It was quick to setup but was definitely a time that you wanted to read the fine manual (RTFM (PG version)). It wasn't as easy to setup as the CISCO WES610N that I purchased at the same time BUT it is also feature rich.

I have had it up for a few days and haven't experienced major problems with it. We will see if it stands up to the test of time and gives me 3-4 years of service like my Cisco Linksys devices that are still working 4 1/2 years later.

Nerd Alert - I am a nerd at heart and utilize geek speak way too often. I try to remember that the Amazon audience contains friends, family, and strangers that may or may not know IT.

PROS:
* Feature Rich -
The ZyXEL is 1/2 the price of the comparable Cisco device but it has a much more feature rich set of wireless capabilities. It supports WPS, allowing for easy setup. It supports WDS, allowing you to configure a network that allows you to carry your laptop from room to room in a large house without sacrificing much speed if setup correctly. It can access as a repeater if needed.

* Cabling -
The ZyXEL includes the power supply and a network cable (CAT-5). It supports a standard called MDI/MDIX, which means that you won't need a crossover cable if you connect it to a switch.
* Wireless Distribution Service -
You can make this part of your existing network using WDS, or Wireless Distribution Service, or simply configure it as an access point. I just removed two old Linksys routers from being WDS nodes since replacing my old Actiontec 802.11a/b/g with an Actiontec 802.11b/g/n wireless router. Eventually I will get around to using the ONI port and setting up a network with DD-WRT

CONS:
* LAN ports on the back are are 10/100 -
While the router notes that it supports connection speeds up to 300MbPS it only has two (2) 10MbPS/100MbPS RJ-45 (LAN) connections. Technically you may never truly realize the full throughput available with this device. This is not unlike other wireless access points, such as the Cisco WET610N (single 10/100) or the Cisco WES610N (quad port 10/100 for $10 more). I did what any good geek would do; used it as an excuse to purchase an 8-port Netgear 10/100/1000 switch to replace my 5-port 10/100 switch in my office/lab with the computers and Hyper-V lab systems. I am going to use the Cisco product downstairs with my home server and VMWare ESXi box.

* Setup may be difficult for the average home user -
I most certainly RTFM'd and reading the manual helped. It did take a quick configuration of my network card in order to even get to the point I could setup the device.
The Cisco devices use an APIPA address, which makes setup easier. Why? APIPA is that 169.254.#.# address that your computer gets when it connects to a network that doesn't give out addresses. This allows you to easily setup the Cisco WES610N.
text_fidelity_b: ZyXEL 300 Mbps Wireless N Access Point, Ethernet Client, Universal Repeater, and Range Extender (WAP3205)

text_fidelity_a:
HAOHUNT Camcorder Digital Video Camera HD 1080P 30fps 3.0 INCH Touch Screen 24MP Camcorder with Microphone and Wide Angle Lens Vlogging Camera with Remote Control Infrared Night Vision Recorder I am impressed right off the bat with just how many useful accessories are included right off the bat. The description says it does not come with an SD card or AAA batteries, but mine did, perhaps for review purposes, although the box did not look like it had been opened. Seems like it would come with that stuff, so perhaps other reviewers might clarify. There is a case and two separate pouches for the wider camera lens and the microphone.

Functionality and video quality are pretty good. I guess the only drawback is that this almost seems like a throwback now. For still pictures - on a vacation or a great hike where I want to take great pictures - I still take along a small camera instead of just my cell phone, but the truth is cell phone cameras are getting so good now that I wonder when that will no longer seem prudent. And with that said, my small camera takes such amazing (not studio quality) HD that I wonder when something like this would really seem like the best thing, especially considering they both take SD cards and length is only limited by SD card capacity.

It certainly does seem like a more professional camera in its size and shape, but mostly because that style has been the trend for some time now. But in a way this style is already starting to seem outdated, like a throwback. I also noticed, just now, that even the really big name manufacturers have this style in 1080p for comparable prices.

I'd definitely give this thing a look. I would have totally loved it a few years ago. The mic and extra lens still feel like premium features, but I'm rarely the one to set up for photos and video footage, as I usually just do landscapes or great spontaneous moments. This may be a fantastic alternative to giving kids your phone - or a phone - to play with. Seems like a good way to encourage their inner photographer without it leading into a bunch of cheap phone games.

Camera has mini* USB and HDMI ports (as opposed to micro) - just when I was wondering what I'd ever do with this one mini-HDMI cable I have... Mic takes 2xCR2032 batteries, which are included, and should probably last, as I don't think mics eat up much power. Has a curled, springy, analogue audio cable with stereo mini-plugs on both ends to connect the mic. Also has an external battery charger.
text_fidelity_b: HAOHUNT Camcorder Digital Video Camera HD 1080P 30fps 3.0 INCH Touch Screen 24MP Camcorder with Microphone and Wide Angle Lens Vlogging Camera with Remote Control Infrared Night Vision Recorder

text_fidelity_a:
WD My Passport 1TB Portable External Hard Drive Storage USB 3.0 Black I give this drive five stars for its size - its physical dimensions - because although I have the same quibbles about it as I do with all other external drives, its size is smaller than other 2.5" external hard drives I've seen, including the 1.5TB Seagate that I own.

In the 2.5" hard drive world - the drives that can run on just USB power - there are internal drives that you can pair with an external case and there are external drives that come in a case and with software - usually a Graphical User Interface (GUI) to help the layman back things up. Unlike the 3.5" hard drive world, capacities are larger earlier in the external devices, but somehow the casing and enclosed bridge (in this case SATA to USB) make the physical size larger than an internal drive with case. This one is still a little bigger, but really quite small. It's awesome, frankly. To have that much capacity in something you can store just about anywhere and you don't even have to mess around with a power cord.

What I don't like - and I complain about this with all external hard drives - is the included software that they want you to install to do backups, etc. As an advanced computer user, I think it's nonsense; even my mother should be able to use the drive without any software. Of course you don't have to use it. The thing that annoys me is that the drive - again, like all other externals nowadays - comes with a sleep timer set, in this case at 30 minutes, so I have to install the interface software to turn that off (necessary for my intended application), and then uninstall the software to get it off my system, but all software leaves a trace after its removal.

If this is your first USB 3.0 peripheral, be aware that the port on the drive is unlike any USB 2.0 port, and thus will require a different cable if you need one longer than the included ~1m cable. More industry stupidity, so they can overcharge for the first year or so. Look for a cheap one on Amazon so you don't have to run out to Best Buy and pay 10x too much. Interface cables are the one thing I believe in buying as cheap as possible - and thank God for Amazon in that respect.

One more note in response to another review: prices on non-solid state hard drives have been fluctuating a lot recently because of the Thai floods, and prices of electronics on Amazon always fluctuate. I typically check all prices before buying anything, but still end up buying from Amazon 99% of the time. I haven't seen Best Buy have a real deal in years. They make their money off lies that their employees tell you, either because they have been brainwashed in to believing said lies or because of commission. Do your own price comparison when the time comes to make a purchase.

The only thing I don't love about this drive is an industry problem that's not going away any time soon, and I have to just stop complaining about it (later). I give this a higher than average review because I was actually surprised - and impressed - with the physical size.
text_fidelity_b: WD My Passport 1TB Portable External Hard Drive Storage USB 3.0 Black

CablesOnline 6ft 2-RCA Male to 2-RCA Female Red/White Audio Extension Cable, (AV-E406RW) These are pretty much as basic an RCA cable you can find that will extend the length of your existing RCA cables without the need for another male-to-male adapter. While for components that have RCA hookups that allow you to use any RCA cable that your can find, I would recommend buying a single longer cable as every connection point is a place for potential signal loss. However, for components that have their RCA cables integrated with the device, you have little choice but to buy an extender such as this. Turntables, especially the older variety, are the most notable components that have this configuration, and since most people like to be able to play records from a location that is easy to reach and has plenty of headroom, this is often far away from your receiver and the built-in cables on the turntable are usually far too short for this. This is why these cables are a perfect way to add an extra 3' while only introducing one additional connection in your linkage, where using a standard RCA cable with a male-to-male adapter introduces two.

Also, since the cables which are connected to turntables are almost always of bare-bones quality with the minimum gauge of copper necessary to carry a signal (that's assuming the wire is made from copper at all, and not from some other cheaper alloy), these are probably going to be the same gauge. Your connection is only as good as the weakest link, so buying some thick gauge cable that is made out of magnetically polarized copper probably would only serve to drive the price up with no actual benefit to you except for being able to brag about them. Therefore, this RCA cable extenders is all that you really need and will spare you the embarrassment of spending money on something that you actually do not need at all. Some "high end" users might complain about them being of a small gauge because they have convinced themselves that they have to use overpriced Monster cables to connect their gear to be able to fully enjoy it., but I don't necessarily buy into this. True, good cable makes a difference, especially when you are sending a signal over a longer distance (10' or more) chances are the mid-grade cable of 16 gauge copper wire with gold plated contacts is all you're going to need. This cable solves your short cable problem while telling the world "I am care about how my music sounds, but I am neither a sucker nor a fool!"
text_fidelity_b: CablesOnline 6ft 2-RCA Male to 2-RCA Female Red/White Audio Extension Cable, (AV-E406RW)

text_fidelity_a:
Pivotal Living Tracker 1 (2nd Generation) Black (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I came to this tracker cold. The Housemate has a Fitbit, but I never used it, and really haven't paid a lot of attention to what it did so I had no expectations of what the Pivotal Living tracker might do. However before I tell you what I discovered, let me explain some things about myself. I'm in my sixties, and have a sedentary job. I would like to be more active, I would like to compare my actual sleep habits against what I perceive them to be, I would like to keep an eye on hydration. I have some other goals, but these are the main ones that apply to my use of the tracker.

So how does the Pivotal Living tracker stand up to these goals? First off, because so much of my everyday movement is not easily measurable by the tracker, I'm not really getting an accurate step count. (Moving around the house holding things doesn't always register. Sitting and doing something like folding laundry sometimes does.) This is a bit of a problem because it makes it difficult to estimate how I'm doing on my step goal. So, accuracy in step count? Not so much. Going to stick to a pedometer or pedometer app. C, maybe C+ because I can set my own goals based on my health and how my day is going. (Right now I have a torn meniscus, and all my steps are limping or cane-assisted. Not fun, and not conducive to accurate step counts.)

Hydration? Great, unless you forget to enter an amount until after midnight. Whoops, sorry, can't add anything to your daily total. This is a huge oversight IMO. I sometimes finish my daily amount late in the evening when I'm not thinking about using the mobile app. However, the process of tracking it on your own is a good one. They simply need to fix the access problem. B+

Daily activity. Honestly I have NO clue how this is tracked. I'd have thought it was step-based, but I've never yet had daily activity show up on my dashboard, so there has to be some other way this band tracks activity. However, having an activity alarm that reminds me to stop what I'm doing, get up and walk around for a few minutes... that's immensely valuable to me. Without it, I'd simply forget and keep on writing or editing. I'm going to give it an A because I love the alarm which can be set for 20/40/or 60 minutes.

The rest? Sleep alarm... I've been wakened by this exactly once, when I was very nearly awake anyway. Every other morning it's done zip. I'll wake up an hour later and think, "Wha?" It's back to my clock radio. C, at best. However the sleep tracker seems surprisingly accurate based on what I remember of my nights. It fairly accurately charts how many times I've woken up, and how much good sleep I've gotten. I find this quite reassuring. A, even A+.

Calories burned: Since this is both step and activity based, it's pretty useless for me. Anyway, my goal isn't about calories, it's about activity, so I'm not going to grade this part of the app. Also, weight: Clearly this is another sub-app like hydration, which requires you to input your numbers. It keeps my weight in front of me which is a good thing, but it's not really something I feel I can adequately grade.

Problem: If you take it off it will turn itself off. I tried to put it on my desk when I was typing since it interfered with the position of my wrist. I could hear the activity alert when the band buzzed against the desk, but then it stopped because the tracker had shut down. I thought it was out of juice and couldn't figure out why I was getting less than 24 hours on the battery. When I finally figured it out, I had to start wearing it up high on my arm. Fortunately the band is big enough to allow it to sit several inches above my wrist.

Price: Very, very good. I recognize that the modest cost of the tracker is intended to get you to buy the yearly subscription, but I don't mind that. If the service works, I'm happy to pay $1 a month for it. That's still minor league stuff. However I get frequent errors saying that the goal information can't be updated from the site, and I get odd readings on my dashboard. However, by the end of the day it's usually sorted itself out, so I don't have a lot of quibbles so far.

Overall, and taking price into account I think I'd give this a B, at least for my needs. It reminds me of the things I need to remember to do, and it gives me a place where I can keep track of those goals. The cost to do this is, as I indicated, quite modest. If you're not ready to drop a lot of money on a more sophisticated tracker, give the Pivotal Living tracker a try.

Note: I'm using this on a Fire phone, which means I had to side-load the app. The instructions on how to install Google Play and everything else you need to side load Google Play apps are available on You Tube, and it's dead easy. Once you've done that, just go to the Play Store and download the Pivotal Living app, and have at it.
text_fidelity_b: Pivotal Living Tracker 1 (2nd Generation) Black (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Sony ICF-SW7600GR AM/FM Shortwave World Band Receiver with Single Side Band Reception After reading reviews and trying to balance everything, i finally got around to making myself order this radio. My intent was to replace my Sangean 909 ATS which has been showing signs of not being as sensitive to DX and SW-SSB stations. After trying .....with the included antenna and several add on antennas i was disappointed to find that this radio was less useful in listening to SW-SSB than the Sangean which has LOTS OF HOURS ON IT. When i could pick up SW-SSB stations the fine tuning never really let me "center" it so that i could listen to the hams talk about their antennas and their dogs. I suppose the Fm and MW were ok although i didn't spend much time trying them, my goal was to buy a good, "hot' portable SW. This one isn't it...perhaps the luck of the draw with some little discreet component or the factory adjustment as it left the shop. Who knows.

Besides that, there is no AC power pack and you will be finding one to pay for extra. The controls are strange, badly laid out and for some things require both hands on the radio to accomplish. Tiny little switches you cannot see without good light on the end almost guarantee your other fingers will hit the 3 button on the front. More controls on the left end....more controls on the front, many with at least two functions per button. And, the slight but noticeable delay between pushing the up or down frequency button and when it really locks on and you get sound again

Had this radio been really sensitive and really pulled in the distant stations or really done a great job on SW-SSB i would have forced myself to deal with the controls. So, i sent it back. Amazon was great and took it with my description of the problems. Perhaps they have taken some back before. SONY...ARE YOU LISTENING??
text_fidelity_b: Sony ICF-SW7600GR AM/FM Shortwave World Band Receiver with Single Side Band Reception

text_fidelity_a:
LENRUE Portable Wireless Bluetooth Speaker with Built-in-Mic,Handsfree Call,AUX Line,TF Card for iPhone Ipad Android Smartphone and More (Grey) I've been wanting my own bluetooth speaker forever. The interesting thing is that I'm not even interested in the bluetooth capability. I want the aux connection for my first generation iPod, which doesn't have bluetooth technology. My iPhone just doesn't have the space for all the music I have on the iPod, plus I don't want to use up data streaming Pandora. Additionally, bluetooth and getting stuff to connect is just a pain. So, I've never tried to connect via bluetooth only the aux.

At first I thought I had dud. I charged it and went to push the power button and nothing happened. I read the tiny print in the instructions and still nothing. So, I went on YouTube to see if anyone made video about using this and of course there is! So, you have to press the power button until the device glows blue and beeps! No where on the instructions does it say to do this! So, once you do this, then you can follow the directions to use the speaker. If you are going to just use the aux plug then push the "M" button, which I think stands for mode. You're good to go.

Now this is tiny, so you're going to get a lot of output, but it what it does put out is a decent sound. I have used mine in a small pavilion for a party and on my front porch. At the party depending on the song, a few downloaded from the early aughts were too quiet to hear, but songs downloaded from iTunes or from CDs came out loud enough to hear throughout the pavilion. Just make sure the volume is up on your speaker AND your device. I've used for about 12 hours total. 4 hours here, 4 hours there, etc., and I still haven't charged it. So it holds a good charge to last through a party or an afternoon lounging on the porch.

You get an aux cord and a USB charging cord. So you can charge it on the computer or with a charger plug that uses a USB plug. The light ring turns red when charging and goes off when it's fully charged. The ring glows blue when it is on. It flashes when it it searching or looking for a bluetooth device. I bought this after a family member refused to let me use his "expensive someone is going to steal it" bluetooth speaker even though he never uses it (and I'm never in a situation to have someone steal it.)
text_fidelity_b: LENRUE Portable Wireless Bluetooth Speaker with Built-in-Mic,Handsfree Call,AUX Line,TF Card for iPhone Ipad Android Smartphone and More (Grey)

text_fidelity_a:
eufy security, SoloCam E40, Outdoor Security Camera, Advanced AI Person-Detection, Two-Way Audio, 2K Resolution, 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi Only, IP65 Weatherproof, No Monthly Fee I contacted Eufy after the battery died after 4 weeks. Took them 2 days to send me an autobot emailed response to which I responded that I wanted a live person to email me. Another 2 days, and a person asked me to send a screen shot of the battery settings. REALLY??? So I did that which my battery settings were for optimized battery life. Another 2 days and still no answer. There was an option on the bottom of their email to escalate the case to management if I was not happy with the response, and that they would get back to me within 24 hours. So I clicked it, and explained how I was not getting a response. But guess what? I never got a response. So five days later, I decided to return this because I'm still in the return window. Maybe I had a defective unit. We have had a very mild winter, so I cannot imagine that the weather would make a supposed four-month battery charge only last for four weeks. Plus, there isn't much motion going on to drain the battery either. Sometimes, 3 or 4 days go by with no motion. The most number of times it has detected motion in one day is four times. So it's not like the battery is getting drained from the camera being triggered 10 times a day. I'm going to try one more time, and watch the battery life to see how quickly it drains before the return window closes.

**** Update **** The replacement camera will have a battery life of approximately 6 or 7 weeks, judging by the amount of battery used thus far. Since the return window is just 4 weeks, I have returned this camera again and will not try another one. 6-7 weeks battery life is better than 4 weeks, for sure. But still disappointing because Eufy advertises a 4 month battery life. I would have been willing to try to Eufy 2 Pro that has a 365-day battery life (figuring it probably really only has a 6 month battery life). But this would mean purchasing a home base. Also, the location of the camera does not get any direct sunlight, so even a solar panel would not have helped. If you are looking for just one camera that is wireless, and you aren't interested in having to take it down every month or two for recharging, this is not the camera for you. Their customer support contacted me the day after I wrote my first review. (I couldn't get any support previously through their normal channels.)
text_fidelity_b: eufy security, SoloCam E40, Outdoor Security Camera, Advanced AI Person-Detection, Two-Way Audio, 2K Resolution, 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi Only, IP65 Weatherproof, No Monthly Fee

Performance is fine for e-books and videos, but sometimes sluggish for intense game playing, photo/video editing or even text editing. The SD card slot lets you store lots of TV shows and movies and use the main memory for apps (which often work poorly if stored on the SD card). Kindle e-books sometimes work much better on the Fire tablets than on ipads or Android tablets, especially if the books have embedded audio or video. The user interface revolves around the books and videos that you bought from Amazon. With a considerable amount of work, you may be able to replace the user interface with a more standard Android launcher that focuses on your apps and files. Realistically, the performance of this tablet clunky enough that I don't recommend it unless you are mostly using it for e-books and videos, so maybe changing the user interface is not worth the effort.

You should also ask yourself if you are using the tablet for mostly e-books and videos, do you really need a 10 inch screen? The 8 inch Kindle Fire tablet has similar performance and a much lower price and is also lighter weight and less bulky, making it easier to use in many situations.
text_fidelity_b: Fire HD 10 Tablet with Alexa Hands-Free, 10.1" 1080p Full HD Display, 32 GB, Marine Blue (Previous Generation - 7th)

A positive review was not required, nor was it requested, and all words are my own.

In 2008, I got a Chevy Cobalt and it came with a great feature:

AUX cable input

That meant I could connect my iPod to the car and listen to my music. But, the problem I’ve been facing is …

The cables.

I seem to go through a ton of them. The last few have been okay, but given the price I’ve paid – not worth it. I’m not particularly rough on cables either. Just seem to use quite a few of them. I’ve been through at least six (6) to seven (7) since I’ve had my car.

These cables, while not super strong, are definitely in the affordable range and provide the same great sound (at least in my car) that expensive ones do. That’s all I really need. The length is both a positive and negative. I’ve found that it is manageable as long as I have the little rubber band that comes with it.

EVOO 14.1” Ultra Thin Laptop FHD, 32GB Storage, 4GB Memory, Micro HDMI, Front Camera, Windows 10 Home I honestly can’t think of an intended user for this laptop. It’s so sluggish that if I gave it to a kid, I can’t imagine them having the patience to wait for the *browser* to open. Let alone go to a website.

I’m a semi-patient adult in my 30s and wanted to chuck this laptop against the wall because the initial setup took so long. For an example, I tried to load the system information to find hardware information, and it took SEVEN seconds to open the Start Menu and load System Information.

The processor is an Intel(R) Celeron(R) CPU N3350 @ 1.10GHz. The laptop has 4GBs of RAM.

My three-year-old phone has 4GB of RAM and is snappier than the EVOO laptop. I have a Chromebook (Acer R11) that is also about three years old, and it’s snappier, too.

Windows 10 S is the default on the laptop, which doesn’t allow you to install any programs not from the Microsoft app store. I suppose that’s useful for basic users, but if you want to put another browser on, you have to disable S mode. Once you disable S mode, you can’t go back to it.

I thought I’d use this laptop for writing, since it’s so slow to load anything that I wouldn’t be tempted to go online. But I don’t even like typing on it; the keyboard feels like I’m typing on a cardboard box. There’s a hollow plastic sound when I type; it’s *that* flimsy. There are some keyboard shortcuts, but I thought it was odd that there wasn’t a shortcut to adjust the brightness. Considering how long it takes the Start Menu to load, that doesn’t make it easy to change the brightness of the screen.

The trackpad is decent, probably the best part of the laptop for me. It has a slightly sandy texture. For an inexpensive laptop, the trackpad isn’t bad.

The laptop is made in China.

TP-Link AC750 Wifi Range Extender | Up to 750Mbps | Dual Band WiFi Extender, Repeater, Wifi Signal Booster, Access Point| Easy Set-Up | Extends Wifi to Smart Home & Alexa Devices (RE200) This review is for the TP-link AC750 Dual Band WiFi Range Extender

I am using this on a network that has a Mac Mini, a couple of iPhones and an iPad. None of these devices could print to both printers; it was one or the other and not both on every single Apple product. After trying everything I could think of, I bought this extender and tried to set it up using the Quick Setup instructions. Anyone EVER had the experience of those Quick Setups working? I haven't and I've been using this stuff for decades. After Quick Setup failed to do anything other than connect to my router and open my network up to anyone that could get signal, I tried a different approach.

The EASIEST WAY TO SET THIS UP is to use the WPS button on your router and on the device. Press the WPS button on the router, then, press the WPS button on the extender. After a minute or so, the router and extender are paired/connected and the result is a secure connection to the router (uses the router's password--you do have a password don't you) with a much stronger signal in what were dead zones. Placement of the extender is sort of an experiment and moving it from plug to plug will show you the best location. Moving the extender after pairing does NOT foul up the connection.

I have two printers, a Samsung M2070W laser and an Epson Eco Tank inkjet. Both have wireless capability and can use WPS setup. To setup other WPS capable devices, just press the WPS button on the ROUTER and then the WPS button on the next device you want to connect. The connection to the router goes through the connected extender with no problem and does not interfere with the router/extender pairing. Do each device one at a time.

This was the solution I needed and now all wireless devices work together. It's a neat solution to solving signal strength and connectivity that can be an enormous hassle when using multiple devices from different makers.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link AC750 Wifi Range Extender | Up to 750Mbps | Dual Band WiFi Extender, Repeater, Wifi Signal Booster, Access Point| Easy Set-Up | Extends Wifi to Smart Home & Alexa Devices (RE200)

text_fidelity_a:
iHome IHM28W2 Color Changing Alarm Clock FM Radio with USB Charging The home is a decent little alarm clock/speaker, though not always the finest in terms of design.

What does it do?
Acts as an alarm. Some people I noted were annoyed that you had to cycle through the minutes to set the time and alarm and while an hour button is easier, if you hold down the button it really zips through pretty quickly. In other words, you really don't have to plod through minute by minute. To give a sense of that, it took me 10 seconds to speed from 6:00 am to 10:00 am. So really, this isn't much of an issue in my mind. It has two alarms, which is a nice touch. The alarm can go to either the radio or to your input device, though that is a bit iffy depending on your device. It worked with my ipod touch but you're going to want to make sure your device works as it should. One problem is that it is not very easy to see in the dark.

Acts as a radio: the reception was quite good; I had no trouble with local stations. All tuned in well.

Acts as a speaker: the sound is decent for what it is. It certainly isn't going to replace your stereo or even a set of decent bluetooth speakers, but that isn't really its goal and for what it's meant to do, and what its probably target audience is (children, tweens, young teen) I'm sure it's fine.

Work with audio devices--this is a bit mixed. I've had variability with a range of Apple products. They all work in terms of producing sound, but the volume varied amongst them at times so that even with the volume all the way up on both devices it was surprisingly low. Not inaudible or anything, but not loud enough for good entertainment (probably OK for an alarm). You also just basically sit your device atop between two plastic "walls"--there's no cradle or anything and so there isn't much difference between that and just lying it flat next to or atop it. It charged my devices, but it's not a charging cradle, which would have been nicer. Instead there is a USB charge slot on the bottom of the device and you use your own charging cable. The same is true for the audio--you use a cable jack into your device (this one is provided) to link the two. It's an adequate design, if not an elegant one.

Glow/change colors: Well, it does do this. My response? Meh. But then, again, I'm really not I'm assuming the target audience. It doesn't do a anything for me, but kids and tweens might find it interesting. At the least, it isn't obnoxious (not too bright, not too fast-changing, etc.)

it's plastic, but it feels pretty hefty and the build seems decent if a little cheap. I certainly didn't have the sense that it would be fragile or break down soon or anything.

in the end, I'd say it's a decent little device for a tween sort. Not sure it's worth 50 dollars, but it's not exorbitant, just maybe a little pricey. If you're just looking for a speaker, I'd say there are bluetooth ones out there that provide better sound for the price. But if you want a speaker/alarm/radio/something to look at now and then, it's a decent purchase.
text_fidelity_b: iHome IHM28W2 Color Changing Alarm Clock FM Radio with USB Charging

It does have a lot of interesting features like the adjustable view angles and finally the best feature is the touch screen. I just wish I knew a way to make it a little brighter. I am still waiting to hear back from them on that.

It really comes with a lot of great accessories including the double battery charger and the many different mount types. As I was saying before this is a good product that could use a little improvement but it excels in a lot of areas also. It's also extremely light when not in the case. The tripod in the photo's doesn't come with the camera it was just attached when I photographed it. As I said before this wasn't the camera for close up still shots but does great while driving and underwater.

This would be great for beginners and people that are just interested in taking quick videos but not for much more then that. For the price though it's a great little back up device and because it's so light and small it's east to take with you.

An update to this review might be pending depending on what I hear from the seller.

text_fidelity_a:
SanDisk Ultra Fit 128GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive - SDCZ43-128G-GAM46 I've always been really happy with SanDisk cards and flash drives, both for speed and reliability, unhesitatingly recommending them vs playing data roulette with generic drives. So I didn't really think twice when I needed to upgrade to a 128GB flashdrive from my smaller ones, I just ordered another SanDisk Ultra Fit.
Oops. No more.
The many other reviews are correct. This drive has serious overheating problems.
It works great if you're not trying to write more than a few GB at a time.
It also works pretty well in an external USB Hub, wrapped in ice packs. But that's not exactly practical, and completely defeats the purpose of getting a small form factor drive in the first place.
It also works okay if I intentionally throttle data transfer 30%-50%, but that's really pretty pointless, isn't it?
So it's not bad for storing data, photos, video, etc., as long as you don't mind setting up ice packs for the initial loading. But useless for backups, hosting virtual machines, sneaker net, or any other data intensive operation.
Basically useless for at least half of what I wanted it for.
And SanDisk's generic response "SanDisk drives comply with industry specific standards and are tested to remain in acceptable temperature ranges under normal operating conditions" is pretty darn useless too.
[Edit] Be aware that when it overheats it starts randomly disconnecting. This will corrupt datafiles being written ***without any warning***. If you care about your data, you need to do a CRC or full binary compare after copying data to this drive.
text_fidelity_b: SanDisk Ultra Fit 128GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive - SDCZ43-128G-GAM46

The main positives - the BT connectivity is excellent and zero loss of signal while jogging/yard work etc. Never had to repair the earbuds to my phone (Note). Battery life is as advertised and very pleasing. Fit is comfortable and no heaviness or blocked feeling.

The could-be-better - getting used to the stem controls is not that easy and has been finicky at times. Volume/bass is mediocre at best. Though some noise reduction is perceivable, it is uneven. It is IPX5 rated, means it should be able to "resist a sustained, low-pressure water jet spray".

At the advertised price, you are paying really for the battery life, BT chip, above-average noise suppression and average sound. Overall, a decent pair for using in situations where you are OK sacrificing performance (travel, yard work, jogging etc - where one could lose or step on it ).

Its performance was good and  the flip microphone made it easy to carry in a holster. Unfortunately it finally died and they are out of production. So I decided to try this headset and was pleasantly surprised. This actually surpasses the Motorola H700. Voice recognition by my iPhone is improved - presumably because of the better noise reduction of the headset, the calls seem very clear on both ends, and the talking caller ID is a real plus.It can fit in the same holster I used for my H700 - though it is a bit large for it. If I can find a holster with a belt clip, this could be a real winner. The only con is that it isn't extremely comfortable on the earlobe after a few hours. The bar that holds the ear clip to the unit is a bit too long I think and the end poking through tends to be a little irritating. It comes with an additional ear pad and clip but there is not really any more comfort using either of those. I have not tried the "comfort kit" - sold separately for way too much money. When I first saw the "comfort kit" advertised I was amused that a $100 bluetooth headset would need an additional expenditure  to be comfortable. However I may be forced to try it if I can't get  the ear clip adjusted properly. Jabra should be embarrassed by this.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra SUPREME Bluetooth Headset - Retail Packaging - Black

text_fidelity_a:
VIDBOX Video Conversion Suite For years I've passed by expensive services offering to convert your old VHS tapes and 8 tracks to DVD. Thanks to this handy little device, there's no need for outside help - you can do it entirely on your own and save yourself lots of money.

Not only is this device easy to set up (if you've ever dubbed VHS tapes, it's roughly the same set-up) but it's compact (the device itself is the same size as a deck of cards). Unlike other gadgets these days, it will work with older Windows operating systems instead of demanding that you download the latest bloatware or update. As if this wasn't enough, you can also convert the music from your audio cassettes and old LPs to a digital format (this is a bonus feature as far as I'm concerned since the product is marketed as primarily a video product). I also liked the fact that you can export the saved file to iTunes and, once ready, can view an old video you made years ago on your iPhone or iPad!

My only quibble is that the editing features aren't as extensive as those programs specifically made for enhancing your old videos, but overall the program provides everything you need to make a smooth transition from copying an old VHS to DVD. Overall I am very happy with this product.
text_fidelity_b: VIDBOX Video Conversion Suite

text_fidelity_a:
Jaybird Freedom Sprint Bluetooth Headphones - Retail Packaging - Midnight Black Overall I'm very pleased with these ear buds. They are my first pair of bluetooth buds and it has been wonderful to not have to deal with cords, especially when working out. I can't tell you how many times I've hit an earbud cord while exercising and ripped the ear bud from my ear. A real pain in the neck (and ear!).

>>>Pros:

Comfort - These fit very well in my ear. There are different tip sizes to create a good fit and, after trying them all out, I went with the medium size. Very comfortable to wear even for long periods of time.

Stay put - I've yet to have them fall out even when doing aerobic exercises or while on the treadmill.

Sound - they sound pretty good. The sound is not as good as my favorite (and inexpensive) corded buds ([[ASIN:B0053R0WWG RHA MA-350 Aluminium Noise Isolating In-Ear Earphones]]) but they are a solid B+ performer with regard to bass response and overall clarity. Keep in mind that good bass response is affected by how the buds fit in your ear, so it's important to try out different tip sizes to see how they affect sound quality. They do get harsh at loud volumes, but for normal listening they are more than fine for my non-audiophile ears. They do reasonably well at blocking out ambient noise.

Setup - I found it straightforward even though I've never had any experience with setting up bluetooth earbuds.

Size - nice and compact so you don't get the "radar dish" look that larger units can have.

Durability - they have a "sweat proof" guarantee which is nice (although I imagine, like most guarantees, there are some loopholes). Overall build quality is good, with a very solid feel to all components.

>>>Cons:

Battery life - The manufacturer claims a battery life of 4.5 hours but I've yet to get more than 3 hours off a single charge. Plus there's no warning about battery life (until you're almost fully discharged) or a visual indicator of how much charge there is left.

Usability - the buttons on the buds are too small, making it difficult for me to push the right one. A lot of fumbling and mis-presses, making it often easier to deal with volume changes on the device, which kills some of the value of having wireless buds. I guess I lack the nimble fingers of the primary target market.

But overall, I'm pleased. The pros outweigh the cons, and I think this is a solid 4-star device.
text_fidelity_b: Jaybird Freedom Sprint Bluetooth Headphones - Retail Packaging - Midnight Black

text_fidelity_a:
Compressed Air Duster, Electronic Air Duster, Portable 40000 RPM Cordless Dust Blower, 6000mAh Battery Air Can Duster, Powerful Computer Keyboard Cleaning Air Spray, Rechargeable Electric Canned Air This air blower is simplistic with no added bells or whistles, but wow is it super powerful! When you push the button you can really feel your hand move from the power of those 40,000 RPMs.
I started using it right out of the box, as it came already charged. It only took seconds to blow out my tower PC. It did such a great job I actually went around blowing the dust off of everything, from the back of the TVs, the tops of all my door frames, and the shelves in my laundry room and pantry until the battery ran out, which was only around 15 minutes.
One of the best things is, is that the charger actually plugs into a wall outlet. There's no USB cord to keep up with and no searching around for an extra brick, which is never included with devices these days. It does take between 2 to 2.5 hours to charge the air blower to only get about 17 minutes of use out of it. For your typical electronic dusting and such, that's a good amount of time, but if you're wanting to use it for dusting other things, that's not long at all.
Overall, this is one powerful beast of an air blower and works great for electronics and regular dusting needs. The low usage time per charge leaves quick work of any of the other advertised uses for this device. Even with that, I still believe this air blower deserves at least 4.5 Stars ✨ and I definitely recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Compressed Air Duster, Electronic Air Duster, Portable 40000 RPM Cordless Dust Blower, 6000mAh Battery Air Can Duster, Powerful Computer Keyboard Cleaning Air Spray, Rechargeable Electric Canned Air

A digital signal especially for anything less than 25 orr 30 feet is a digital signal and as long as the cable is connected to the HDMI ends you get the same quality of 0/1 as you do with a ridiculously priced cable. I ordered both HDMI and Fiber Toslink cables from this branded manufacturer and they came packaged nicely and safely to prevent damage in transit with the UPS monsters and are performing perfectly. I actually did pay over $50.00 for a six-foot HDMI cable at Best Buy and all I can say is that I must have had a lot of money to waste as this brand is equally as reliable and I could have purchased twenty of these for the price of the one Monster at Best Buy. The only people who will argue these points are snobs who think there is some sort of prestige associated with having over priced digital cables. If this was for speakers or other copper reliant products I would at least partially agree that high-quality is very important but even there we are still getting products shipped mainly from China that have the fancy packaging and marketing hype attached to them and you can do a lot better shopping for solid quality without all the needless BS. But these and you will be pleased. SS

text_fidelity_a: Selore&S-Global USB C to Dual HDMI Adapter 4K @60hz, Type C to HDMI Converter for MacBook Pro Air 2020/2019/2018,LenovoYoga 920/Thinkpad T480,Dell XPS 13/15,etc… I’ve had this for 8 months with no issues, then I got an under-the-desk treadmill and the screens go black and immediately come back on ALL THE TIME. I’ve tried using different plug ins for the treadmill and computer, not it (my husband is an electrician and assured me this was not it.). When testing this theory and intentionally removing power and plugging back in, the monitor had a setting box pup-up…. Because it lost powder, great. But when the screen flashes that box doesn’t come up which tells me it’s not loosing power-it’s loosing a connection to the computer. After messing with it and becoming frustrated, I thought I heard a little zap noise where it’s located so when I started feeling around I got a very minor static shock on my finger. So my Inspector Gadget hat told me that I was generating static electricity with my treadmill and for some reason it was collecting on this dual monitor plug and basically shorting itself out. (This only happens when walking on the treadmill.) So, in all my Mom-knowing madness, I wrapped it up in a dryer sheet and it actually works for the most part. It might flash a couple times in a day but my office smells amazing. I will be looking for something else for sure. It’s really annoying.

text_fidelity_a: WYZE Cam 1080p HD Indoor Smart Home Camera with Night Vision, 2-Way Audio, Compatible with Alexa & the Google Assistant Bulbs and outlet are OK. I would not buy separately though, as nowadays you get higher quality bulbs and outlets for a discount price.  The sensor bridge, contact and motion sensors are problematic to say the least. I have 2 contact sensors and 3 motion sensors connected to the sensor bridge. Right now all of them are offline, they started going offline one by one. Distance from the sensors to the bridge is not an issue since two of them are located no more than three feet away from the bridge. This is not the first time this has happened. The only solution for me has been to reset bridge and sensors, and reinstall them one by one. Many people complain about the same issue, and this keeps happening. The camera where the bridge is attached is installed 7 ft from the ground, so it has been very aggravating to have to get a ladder every time one of these switches has gone offline. Regarding the camera, you probably will not find anything cheaper in the market right now. This model in particular offers continuous recording provided you insert a storage card, that is a plus. Person detection is back, however sometimes it takes more than 10 minutes to receive a notification. Some people has reported that it has take up to one hour to get the notification. I personally would not recommend getting this package due to the unreliability of the bridge and motion and contact sensors. This is definitely not a system you want to buy to secure your home. The camera can be purchased separately for about $25. The video quality is acceptable during the daytime. If you want a hobby camera, you will not find a better deal. For security purposes, you are better off looking somewhere else.
text_fidelity_b: WYZE Cam 1080p HD Indoor Smart Home Camera with Night Vision, 2-Way Audio, Compatible with Alexa & the Google Assistant

It streams exactly the same as far as I can tell, but it streams very well. It was a bit of a pain to install since the Roku site refused my password and the instructions afterwards aren't all that easy to follow if you lose your password. But, after plugging in all my passwords for internet connection, Netflix, Amazon, etc...it finally started streaming again. I can't tell that it's any faster. Nonetheless, if you don't have a Roku and want to stream a boatload of free channels with movies and lots of other cool stuff to watch, I suggest getting a Roku. You can add paid channels later. And Roku doesn't require a credit card to use.

It comes with a short HDMI cable and everything you need to get streaming. As far as the actual hardware installation, it's extremely easy. It takes less than 10 seconds to put it on top of the TV and connect the 2 cables (HDMI and power). A sticky tape comes to adhere the Roku to the top of the TV since the Roku is so small it tends to fall off with being stuck. This is my 3rd Roku and we rarely watch regular TV anymore.
This Roku will stream in 1080 and 720 psi. I had ordered about 5 or so generic Roku remotes earlier this year since we tend to lose them and one of our dogs has chewed up the original remotes beyond usage, and they all work fine with this Roku.

Roku is always good, just a little bit of a pain to get past all the passwords, codes and stuff in the beginning, especially if your old password for some reason doesn't work anymore.

text_fidelity_a:
Sonpre Samurai Max-C Pop-up SD Rechargeable Speaker for Smartphones/Laptops/Tablets/MP3s - Black This is a more upscale version of the “pop up” speakers that have been around for a while. It adds some useful features including an SD card slot to play mp3 files directly and more advanced controls, such as a toggle switch for track skip and a mute button.

When compressed it’s very compact, measuring roughly 2.5 inches in diameter. While it can be played in its compact mode, the sound quality is not all that great – very tinny with little bass.

The sound quality improves significantly when it’s popped open. That increases the height to about 3.25 inches. That doesn't seem like much, but it makes a huge difference in sound quality. The bass is far more pronounced and, while the mid and upper ranges are still somewhat muddy, it’s far more pleasant to listen to than when it is folded up.

Given the size, I’d rate the sound quality as very good when it is in its pop-up mode. This is not a room-filling speaker but it sounds a whole lot better than the internal speakers in a tablet.

It is a direct-connect only speaker – it does NOT have bluetooth. It comes with a 3.5mm cord that is permanently attached to the base of the speaker. The cable can be stowed in a grove on the base of the speaker. The attached cable is a plus and a minus: you’ll never forget to bring a cable along, but the cord is only about 5 inches long, which made it backward to use on some of my equipment. I like that the cord is attached, but it really needs to be a bit longer.

The build quality feels pretty solid. It’s all plastic, as expected, but it has a nice feel to it. The bellows section in the middle feels like it is build solid enough to last a while. Plus, the fact that you can close it up easily for transport gives me some measure of assurance that it will survive being tossed around a bit. For the price, I’d rate the build quality as very good.

There are less expensive pop-up speakers available, such as the Xboom. I have one of those as well, and when comparing the two side-by-side I thought the sound quality was bit better on the Sonpre. The Sonpre also has more features than the Xboom (the mute button in particular is a welcome addition) and has longer battery life. So, while it is a few bucks more, it does bring some additional features to the table.

Although the short cord drops my rating by a star, this is definitely one to consider if you’re looking for a decent sounding pop-up speaker.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Sonpre Samurai Max-C Pop-up SD Rechargeable Speaker for Smartphones/Laptops/Tablets/MP3s - Black

Byron Statics Portable CD Boombox with AM/FM Radio, Top Loading CD, 1W RMS x 2 Stereo Speaker, Aux-in Jack, LCD Display, AC110-120V Operated (KBB-250) I’m old enough to remember the old 8-track players, but growing up my media player was of course a cassette player, and sometimes a “dual” player.

But, in 1995, I opted to transition to CDs. By that time they were a bit more affordable, though the average $17.95 felt like it was anything but.

By around 2005, I was transitioning to an MP3 player. The first one was a literal BRICK (Creative Nomad).

And, by 2008, I had an iPod Nano. By 2011, I had the iPod classic. Even my 2008 Chevy had an aux port to connect my iPod to. So, I really had NO need of a CD player. After all, most of my music was on my computer or iPod. Living in an apartment is NOT ideal for a “stereo”. I wouldn’t want to hear someone else’s music, so I don’t think they’d want to hear mine.

When I saw this, I decided to get it.

It is COMPACT, no frills, no remote control. In fact there is only a “selection” button, not a (back track or forward track).

I haven’t tried the radio function yet. The CD top loader consists of a manual opening (no push-button), and the CD has to be popped in and out manually. The sound is pretty decent for the size of the unit. This is more for desktop or bedside use. Definitely not for a home “sound system”.

I then tested the AUX cable for the iPod and the sound was the same as the CD. That feature was REALLY easy to use.

It is a pretty solid, light-weight unit. I do believe it could be a bit cheaper. I wouldn’t mind getting a second one should the price drop.
text_fidelity_b: Byron Statics Portable CD Boombox with AM/FM Radio, Top Loading CD, 1W RMS x 2 Stereo Speaker, Aux-in Jack, LCD Display, AC110-120V Operated (KBB-250)

text_fidelity_a: comiso Wireless Earbuds Bluetooth Headphones, True Wireless in Ear Bluetooth 5.1 Earbuds with Microphone, Deep Bass, IPX7 Waterproof Loud Voice Earphones for Sport Outdoor Running Gym Workout(Black) I'm on my third set of budget earbuds and these are far and away the best ones that I've had. The design allows for them to stay on my ears whether I'm running or doing lifting. The battery life is pretty good, I typically use them for between 60 and 90 minutes at a go and I only charge the case every week to 2 weeks depending. The absolute best thing about these is they don't lose connection when you walk more than 7 ft away or when they're sync to your wrist and you only have the right earbud in. That was a common problem when using my garment on my left hand and running with only the right earbud in and other brands. But this one keeps connection the whole time when I'm running no issues. The sound isn't amazing, but it's still good enough that I would only notice it if I grabbed another much more expensive set of headphones to compare it to. Highly recommend for the price
text_fidelity_b: comiso Wireless Earbuds Bluetooth Headphones, True Wireless in Ear Bluetooth 5.1 Earbuds with Microphone, Deep Bass, IPX7 Waterproof Loud Voice Earphones for Sport Outdoor Running Gym Workout(Black)
